docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • This datasheet serves to document the engineering design and implementation process of the distance-sensing subsystem for Project SBWB (Self-Balancing Work Bench).

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
Project SBWB is an automated, self-stabilizing platform designed to maintain a level working surface in dynamic or unstable environments, enabling users to perform precise operations without mechanical interference. The distance-sensing unit operates as a core feedback mechanism alongside an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). While the IMU tracks tilt and velocity, the distance-sensing subsystem continuously measures surface height displacement and positional orientation relative to the base. This spatial data is conditioned, filtered, and transmitted across the microcontroller network to drive motor actuators for active, real-time stabilization.

docs.text:
This Block Diagram shows the lighting sensor of Team SBWB's electrical system. It uses a lighting sensor and some math to determine the currently angle of the table, and then communicates with a teammate's board to rotate clockwise, rotate counter clockwise, or not rotate at all.

The Block Diagram shows the critical wiring of components to the microcontroller and microcontroller peripherals, to document the necessary details of the system for communication and replication purposes.

docs.title: Component Selection Example
docs.text:
Also acceptable, more markdown friendly

Optical Sensing & Distance Detection

  1. Vishay TEFT4300 Photodiode & TSAL6200 IR Emitter Pair

    • $0.85 / pair
    • Vishay TEFT4300 / TSAL6200 Product Link
    Pros Cons High optical sensitivity matched at 950 nm peak wavelength Separate emitter and receiver require precise mechanical alignment on PCB Standard 5mm through-hole package for easy breadboard setup Susceptible to high ambient infrared light without proper shielding Documented switching times for fast object detection

  2. Long Distance Reflective Switch OPB732

    • $4.61 / unit
    • OPB732 Optical Sensor Product Link
Pros Cons Combines an infrared emitter and phototransistor in a single pre-mounted housing Higher unit cost ($2.85) compared to discrete pairings Factory-aligned optics eliminate manual positioning errors on the PCB Fixed focal distance limits flexibility in custom detection ranges Standardized mounting holes for straightforward mechanical integration Limited to close-range reflective detection

  1. Everlight ITF8403 Integrated Reflective Sensor

    • $0.92 / unit
    • Everlight ITF8403 Product Link
    Pros Cons Combines IR emitter and phototransistor in a single 4-pin module Fixed detection range (typically under 15 mm ideal operating distance) Fixed alignment eliminates positioning errors Surface-mount footprint requires careful soldering Integrated daylight blocking filter reduces ambient light noise

Choice: Option 1: Vishay TEFT4300 Photodiode & TSAL6200 IR Emitter Pair

Rationale: Option 1 is the optimal choice for our custom distance sensing subsystem. It provides a discrete solution that allows complete control over the photodiode biasing and gain stage in our custom signal conditioning circuit. Unlike Option 3, which integrates all processing internally, Option 1 satisfies the assignment requirement to implement a custom electrical solution using discrete analog components while keeping unit costs below $1.00.

Signal Conditioning & Amplification

  1. Texas Instruments LM358P Dual Op-Amp

    • $0.45 / unit
    • TI LM358P Product Link
    Pros Cons Low unit cost and widely available 8-pin DIP package Slower slew rate (0.3 V/µs) and limited bandwidth (0.7 MHz) Operates reliably from a single 3V to 32V supply rail Output cannot swing completely rail-to-rail without load resistors Common-mode input range includes ground, enabling direct sensing near 0V

  2. Texas Instruments LM393P Dual Differential Comparator

    • $0.42 / unit
    • TI LM393P Product Link
    Pros Cons Dedicated comparator IC optimized for fast digital output switching Open-collector output requires an external pull-up resistor Open-collector output allows level shifting between logic voltage levels Cannot be configured as a linear amplifier if analog gain is required later Extremely low quiescent current consumption (~0.4 mA per package)

  3. Microchip MCP6002-I/P Dual Rail-to-Rail Op-Amp

    • $0.55 / unit
    • Microchip MCP6002-I/P Product Link
    Pros Cons Full rail-to-rail input and output swing on 1.8V to 6V supplies Maximum operating supply voltage is limited to 6.0V Very low quiescent current (100 µA per channel) Slightly higher unit cost than standard LM358P 1 MHz gain bandwidth product suitable for DC/low-frequency sensing

Choice: Option 1: Texas Instruments LM358P Dual Op-Amp

Rationale: The LM358P is selected because it provides two independent operational amplifiers in a breadboard-friendly 8-DIP package at a very low price. In our IR proximity circuit, one stage can serve as an analog buffer/preamplifier for the photodiode signal while the second stage functions as a voltage comparator against a potentiometer threshold, providing both analog and digital outputs to the microcontroller.

Power Regulation

  1. STMicroelectronics L7805CV

    • $1.08 / unit
    • ST L7805CV Product Link
    Pros Cons Delivers up to 1.5A continuous output current High dropout voltage (~2.0V) requires input voltage at or above 7.0V Built-in thermal overload and short-circuit protection Linear power dissipation generates heat at higher current draws TO-220 package allows easy attachment of a heatsink if needed

  2. Microchip MIC29151-5.0WT Low-Dropout Regulator

    • $4.96 / unit
    • Microchip MIC29151-5.0WT Product Link
    Pros Cons Very low dropout voltage (350 mV at 1.5A load) Significantly higher cost ($4.96/unit) Built-in enable pin for logic-level shutdown 5-pin TO-220 package requires extra board layout connections Reverse battery protection improves system durability

  3. Texas Instruments LM317T Adjustable Regulator

    • $0.82 / unit
    • TI LM317T Product Link
    Pros Cons Adjustable output voltage from 1.25V to 37V Requires two external feedback resistors to set output voltage to 5.0V Up to 1.5A output current capability Higher susceptibility to output voltage drift if resistor tolerances vary Low unit cost

Choice: Option 1: STMicroelectronics L7805CV

Rationale: The L7805CV is the optimal choice for our fixed 5.0V logic and sensor rail. It requires no external voltage setting resistors (unlike the LM317T), provides standard built-in short-circuit and thermal protection, and handles total system current with substantial margin at a low unit cost.

*Power Sources

  1. CUI Inc. SWI12-9-N-P5 9V DC Wall Adapter

    • $8.45 / unit
    • CUI SWI12-9-N-P5 Product Link
    Pros Cons Delivers regulated 9V DC up to 1.33A (12W total power) Tethered to AC wall outlet, limiting physical mobility Ideal 9V output keeps input voltage close to 7V dropout limit of L7805CV, minimizing heat Requires standard 2.1mm DC barrel jack connector on board Continuous operation without battery maintenance

  2. Tensility 16-00142 12V DC Wall Adapter

    • $8.52 / unit
    • Tensility 16-00142 Product Link
    Pros Cons Higher 12V output voltage provides robust headroom for external subsystems Higher voltage drop across the L7805CV regulator generates more thermal heat Provides up to 18W (1.5A) of continuous power capacity Larger physical wall-wart enclosure size Inexpensive at $8.52 per unit

  3. MG Electronics LBP-124500 12V Rechargeable Lithium-Ion Battery Pack

    • $49.95 / unit
    • MG Electronics LBP-124500 Product Link
    Pros Cons Fully portable 12V DC power source enables untethered system operation Significantly higher unit cost ($49.95) compared to wall adapters Includes built-in multi-chemistry rechargeable cells and output leads Requires periodic recharging and eventual battery pack replacement Steady voltage output suitable for regulated linear circuits Adds substantial weight to the overall assembly

Choice: Option 2: Tensility 16-00142 12V DC Wall Adapter

Rationale: The 12V wall adapter is selected as the optimal power source because it provides a reliable, tethered desktop power supply with a higher input voltage headroom (12V) compared to a 9V source. This ensures sufficient input stability above the L7805CV linear regulator's dropout threshold while supporting up to 1.5A of continuous current, meeting all system power demands without requiring battery maintenance.
